limitations: The score measures how well the resume text aligns with this job description. It is not a probability of being interviewed or hired.
Skills are recognised from a curated taxonomy. Technologies outside the taxonomy are only matched when you add them as custom requirements.
A skill that is missing from the resume does not mean the candidate lacks it - only that the document does not show it.
Semantic similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) measures how related two pieces of text are, not competence. Passages longer than ~256 word pieces are truncated by the model.
Experience duration is estimated from date ranges found in the experience section and may be inaccurate for unusual date formats.
Education and certification requirements are reported for manual review and are not part of the numeric score.
The analysis is designed for English-language resumes and job descriptions.

methodology.title: Keyword matching vs. semantic similarity
methodology.body: Keyword matching recognises explicit skills (with aliases such as 'Postgres' → PostgreSQL) and is the only way a skill is credited. Semantic similarity compares the meaning of sentences using a sentence-embedding model and cosine similarity, so 'built REST endpoints' can align with 'develop RESTful services' even without shared keywords. Semantic similarity informs alignment scores but never credits a specific skill on its own.

methodology.title: Component weights
methodology.body: Required skills 35%, preferred skills 10%, semantic similarity 20%, project relevance 15%, experience alignment 10%, evidence strength 10%. Components that do not apply are excluded and their weight is redistributed proportionally.

methodology.title: Credit rules
methodology.body: Each requirement counts once. An explicit match earns full credit; a related but distinct technology earns 40% partial credit; ambiguous or missing evidence earns none. Preferred requirements count 50% as much as required ones where they are combined. 'A or B' requirements are satisfied by either option.

methodology.title: Similarity calibration
methodology.body: Raw cosine similarities are linearly rescaled from [0.2, 0.7] to [0, 100] and clamped. Statements are classed as strong (≥ 0.55), moderate (≥ 0.4) or weak alignment.

methodology.title: Determinism and versioning
methodology.body: Results are deterministic for the same inputs, model, taxonomy and scoring version 1.0.0. The version identifiers are stored with every saved analysis so older reports remain interpretable.
